summary: A [national digital strategy for 2025-2030](2025-05-28-wearetech-togo-digital-strategie-2025-2030) reached consultant procurement with no adoption reported, under a [government roadmap](2026-08-01-togo-vision-2040-deep-dive-secteur-prive) whose text is not held.
developments:
Neither the 2020 strategy nor the 2025-2030 draft is held, and the base does not settle whether the two names denote one instrument or two ([strategy](2025-05-28-wearetech-togo-digital-strategie-2025-2030), [toolbox](2026-06-10-atd-boite-outils-digitaux-tpme)).

The roadmap for 2026-2031 is present only through the government's own account of a private-sector contribution workshop convened under it; the government said it would specify by the end of 2026 the reciprocal commitments it will offer the private sector ([roadmap](2026-08-01-togo-vision-2040-deep-dive-secteur-prive), [financing](2026-08-03-ecofin-togo-secteur-prive-financement-vision-2040)).

Two overarching instruments, neither readable, is the frame against which every delivery below has to be read.

summary: The [electronic communications and posts regulator](2026-07-31-togo-michel-yaovi-galley-head-of-arcep-togo) was created in October 2020 in an institutional reform replacing its predecessor.
developments:
The creation date is held at month precision, and a claim that the country's framework is a model for other African markets is the publisher's and uncorroborated ([regulator](2026-07-31-togo-michel-yaovi-galley-head-of-arcep-togo), [broadband](2026-04-21-artao-ppp-haut-debit)).

The regulator is the most active institution in this ledger — it runs the frequency plan, the fee decrees, the consumer tour and the quality regime — and no annual report, budget or enforcement series for it is held.

summary: A [decree approving the national frequency allocation plan](2026-03-11-togo-decret-2026-037-pnaf) was adopted in March 2026 and published by the regulator in April.
developments:
The decree was adopted in Council of Ministers on 11 March 2026 and published on 15 April; the superseded 2022 decree is not held and carries no exact date in the base ([plan](2026-03-11-togo-decret-2026-037-pnaf), [royalties](2026-07-31-togo-ajuste-reglementation-redevances-radioelectriques-innovation-connectivite)).

A frequency allocation plan adopted and published is the most concrete piece of connectivity policy this unit produced in the period, and no assignment, auction or award has followed it on the record.

summary: A [personal data protection law of ninety-seven articles](2019-10-29-togo-loi-2019-014-protection-donnees-caractere-personnel) was gazetted in October 2019, and what moved in the period is the base's holding of it rather than the instrument.
developments:
The law was gazetted on 29 October 2019 and the gazette's own signature block is dated a day after the title date ([law](2019-10-29-togo-loi-2019-014-protection-donnees-caractere-personnel), [implementation](2023-12-21 ISR - WURI Phase 2 Seq 06 (P169594))).

The instrument did not move in the window. It is the statute that created the protection authority by an article rather than by a separate constitutive act, and it is the basis for the corporate correspondents programme recorded separately.

summary: An [anti-money-laundering law](2025-12-30 Togo Adopts New Law to Strengthen Anti-Money Laundering Rules) was adopted in the December 2025 budget session, with no promulgation date, number or gazette reference held.
developments:
The source gives only the budget session, so the vote date is not established ([law](2025-12-30 Togo Adopts New Law to Strengthen Anti-Money Laundering Rules)).

It is the only payments-adjacent statute in this ledger, and its text cannot be read. Against six institutions live on the regional instant payment platform and a treasury prepaid card announced, the governing law is present as a headline.

summary: [Rules on mobile commercial offers](2026-07-22-maroc-telecom-rapport-financier-semestriel-2026) entered into force in April 2026, recorded in one line of an operator parent's half-year financial report.
developments:
No instrument number, title or text is held, and the sole account is a single line in a foreign-listed operator's financial filing ([rules](2026-07-22-maroc-telecom-rapport-financier-semestriel-2026)).

A rule that changes what operators may offer consumers, evidenced only in the accounts of the company it binds, is worth recording as exactly that. The consumer-rights tour recorded separately is running in the same period with no reference to it on file.

summary: A [review of the 2009 civil registration law](2026-08-24-togo-civil-registration-law-review-togofirst) held its scoping meeting, with proposals due before the end of 2026.
developments:
The scoping meeting was held in August 2026 ([review](2026-08-24-togo-civil-registration-law-review-togofirst)).

It is the statute under which the birth-registration catch-up campaigns and the online certificate pilot operate, and the review is the first movement on it the base holds. No draft or proposal is on record.

summary: A [decree instituting a national conformity-assessment mechanism](2026-07-31-togo-conseil-des-ministres-30-juillet-2026-communique) was adopted in July 2026 with no number, text or entry-into-force date held, at the same session as a [fee and royalty amendment](2026-07-31-togo-conseil-des-ministres-30-juillet-2026-communique).
developments:
The conformity decree was adopted in Council of Ministers on 30 July 2026 and nothing about its content is published ([decree](2026-07-31-togo-conseil-des-ministres-30-juillet-2026-communique)).

The 2023 electronic-communications fees and royalties decree had one annex table amended at the same session; the held copy is an image scan with no text layer, so the rate tables are not machine-readable ([fees](2023-04-05-togo-decret-2023-040-frais-redevances-communications-electroniques), [amendment](2026-07-31-togo-conseil-des-ministres-30-juillet-2026-communique)).

Two instruments adopted in one session, neither readable, is a recurring condition in this unit rather than an accident of one meeting.

2026-08-31 — the National Accounting Council was launched in Lomé, the body a regional directive of 28 November 1997 requires each member state to establish, tasked with making accounting information reliable, comparable and consistent with international standards ([launch](2026-08-31-togofirst-national-accounting-council), [directive](1997-11-28-uemoa-directive-03-97-conseil-national-comptabilite)). Twenty-nine years between the obligation and the institution is the finding; unlike the two July decrees, this one has a named text behind it.

summary: The [data-protection authority](2025-03-29-ipdcp-demarre-activites) formally launched activities with a public campaign from April 2025, and [signed a cooperation accord with the broadcasting authority](2025-12-12 Personal data and digital rights in Togo - HAAC and IPDCP seal institutional cooperation accord).
developments:
The authority was created by an article of the 2019 statute rather than by a separate constitutive act, launched activities at the capital, certified a first cohort of corporate correspondents and held a second edition of a personal-data forum in July 2026 ([launch](2025-03-29-ipdcp-demarre-activites), [correspondents](2026-06-25-ipdcp-forme-premiers-correspondants), [forum](2026-07-29-togofirst-data-protection-forum-lome), [edition](2026-07-29-togo-ipdcp-deuxieme-edition-forum-protection-donnees-personnelles)).

The accord with the broadcasting authority was signed in December 2025; the sole account is sourced to the data-protection authority itself and carries no critical framing of that access ([accord](2025-12-12 Personal data and digital rights in Togo - HAAC and IPDCP seal institutional cooperation accord)).

No enforcement action, penalty, complaint volume or registration count is published at any date.

summary: A [regional dialogue on border interoperability](2026-08-14-togo-ghana-ecowas-enbic-sigmat-border-interoperability) was held at a joint border post, with no data-protection arrangement stated for the shared border and transit data.
developments:
The dialogue took place in August 2026 at a joint post on the coastal corridor ([dialogue](2026-08-14-togo-ghana-ecowas-enbic-sigmat-border-interoperability)).

No deployment figure, timetable or data-protection arrangement for the shared border and transit data is stated. The country has a data-protection statute and an operating authority, and neither is named in the arrangement.

summary: [Transposition of the regional consumer-protection directive](2025-03-24 Togo Adopts WAEMU Consumer Protection Framework) has reached consultation only, a stakeholder workshop in March 2025 with no adoption instrument.
developments:
The source's headline says the framework was adopted and its body describes a workshop; the base has already corrected that ([workshop](2025-03-24 Togo Adopts WAEMU Consumer Protection Framework)).

Nothing since. The consumer-rights outreach tour recorded separately runs on the regulator's existing powers rather than on a transposed directive.

summary: A [free-roaming arrangement with two neighbours](2026-04-27-techreviewafrica-senegal-togo-benin-free-roaming) took effect in April 2026, about four months late against the regional deadline.
developments:
It was signed at the capital and took effect on 24 April 2026 under a regional regulation of December 2017 ([roaming](2026-04-27-techreviewafrica-senegal-togo-benin-free-roaming), [borders](2026-04-26-benin-senegal-togo-roaming-sans-frontieres), [strategy](2024-10-09-ecowas-19th-ministerial-meeting-adopts-digital-sector-development-strategy)).

No traffic or price effect has been published. A regulation adopted in 2017 and applied in 2026 is the measure of how long regional harmonisation takes to reach a subscriber here.

summary: An [African centre for coordination and research in cybersecurity](2026-04-01-watra-cybersecurity-working-group-final-report) is named as the strategic culmination of a bilateral programme, and the country is a founding government of a [pan-African language artificial-intelligence coalition](2026-07-31-gsma-atlas-umoja-ai-launch).
developments:
Chad drew on the Togolese experience of deploying agricultural digital solutions ([visit](2026-09-01-togoofficiel-fsrp-agri-numerique-tchad-visite)).

The cybersecurity centre is named in a regional working-group report which gives no host, no date, no budget and no constituting instrument ([centre](2026-04-01-watra-cybersecurity-working-group-final-report)).

The language coalition launched at a continental telecommunications conference with the digital ministry a founding government; no national deliverable, budget, dataset commitment or timetable is on file, and the base holds no statement on how it relates to the country's own fifty-language project ([coalition](2026-07-31-gsma-atlas-umoja-ai-launch), [declaration](2026-07-24-gsma-abuja-declaration-meaningful-connectivity-atlas-umoja), [initiative](2026-07-28-la-gsma-lance-une-initiative-pour-developper-l-ia-en-langues-africaines)).

summary: A [digital acceleration project](2024-12-18-wb-tgo-001-togo-digital-acceleration-project) has disbursed US$13,992,856 of US$100,000,000, and an [additional US$20,000,000](2026-07-17-togo-world-bank-vision-2040-financement) was signed for the identity programme inside a five-agreement package.
developments:
The disbursement is a single portal point rather than a series, and the government told project coordinators in July 2026 that disbursement rates would no longer count as performance ([project](2024-12-18-wb-tgo-001-togo-digital-acceleration-project), [funding](2024-12-18 Togo - $100 Million in Funding to Accelerate Digital Transformation)).

The identity top-up was signed in July 2026 inside a package of US$429,000,000 ([top-up](2026-07-17-togo-world-bank-vision-2040-financement)); the implementation report gives a phase-two closing date of 30 July 2026 and no held source restates or extends it alongside the top-up ([top-up](2026-07-17-togo-world-bank-vision-2040-financement), [identity](2026-01-01-world-bank-tgo-2026-wuri-digital-id-top-up-bw15), [regional](2024-03-06 1 step forward, 3 steps back for West Africa's regional digital ID projects)).

A public administration service-delivery modernisation project is named as live at the same portfolio review, and the base holds the name and nothing else ([modernisation](2026-07-30-togo-gouvernement-renforce-suivi-projets-banque-mondiale)). A financial governance programme closed at the end of June 2026, digitisation being one component rather than its purpose ([governance](2026-05-20-togo-giz-projet-bonne-gouvernance-financiere-cloture)).

summary: Two phases of [electronic-governance support to the financial administration](2025-01-01-kfw-tgo-001-e-governance-fur-effiziente-finanzverwaltung-ii-efficient) run to 2028, the second financing fibre extension and the connection of town halls, hospitals and schools.
developments:
The second phase was committed in 2025 and finances fibre extension and the connection of town halls, hospitals and schools ([second phase](2025-01-01-kfw-tgo-001-e-governance-fur-effiziente-finanzverwaltung-ii-efficient)), the first in 2024 ([first phase](2024-01-01-kfw-tgo-002-e-governance-fur-effiziente-finanzverwaltung)), both at year precision and both running to 2028.

A bilateral digital transformation programme was committed in 2022 and runs to 2028 ([bilateral](2022-01-01-bmz-tgo-001-digitale-transformation-digital-transformation-in-togo)).

Every financing in this unit is external. No domestic appropriation for digital transformation appears anywhere in the ledger, which is the limit on what this indicator can say about sustainability.

summary: A [EUR 50,000,000 senior loan](2024-01-01-ifc-tgo-001-axian-togo-togocom-telecom-expansion-loan) plus up to EUR 72,000,000 mobilised is the largest private telecoms financing in the country.
developments:
The loan started in May 2024 and is recorded active and invested; the disbursed figure and the 2034 end year are base-imputed patches rather than lender-reported ([loan](2024-01-01-ifc-tgo-001-axian-togo-togocom-telecom-expansion-loan)).

It is the only private-capital instrument of scale in this ledger, and its terms are known through a development finance institution's record rather than through either party.

summary: An [indicative cooperation programme with Luxembourg for 2026-2031](2026-07-21-togo-luxembourg-appui-transformation-numerique-cybersecurite) was signed in a three-accord package carrying EUR 78,550,000, including a [cybersecurity programme](2026-07-21-togo-luxembourg-appui-transformation-numerique-cybersecurite).
developments:
The programme was signed at the capital alongside two other accords; the euro is the announcing currency, the dollar figure in circulation is a publisher's rounding rather than a dated conversion, and the two accounts date the signing a day apart ([programme](2026-07-21-togo-luxembourg-appui-transformation-numerique-cybersecurite), [accords](2026-07-16-togo-luxembourg-accords-cybersecurite), [record](2026-01-01-luxembourg-development-cooperation-tgo-2026-digital-cyber-accords-bw15)).

The cybersecurity component's digital and cyber share of the package is not separately quantified ([cyber](2026-07-21-togo-luxembourg-appui-transformation-numerique-cybersecurite), [agreement](2026-07-16-togo-luxembourg-accords-cybersecurite)).

A card and merchant partnership with a global payment network names the country among five markets; it is company-announced through a press wire and the principals' own release is not held ([card](2025-11-29-axian-mastercard-digital-payments-partnership-techreviewafrica)).

summary: [Fifth-generation service on 100 MHz](2026-04-01-watra-5g-deployment-and-policy-framework) has been commercial since 2020, restated in a regional regulators' survey, and a [licence for internet-of-things networks](2026-08-05-les-grandes-decisions-du-conseil-des-ministres-du-4-aout-2026) was authorised by decree.
developments:
The fifth-generation launch date is held at year precision, and both sources are regional reports faceted to West Africa, so a national query misses them ([service](2026-04-01-watra-5g-deployment-and-policy-framework), [report](2026-04-01-watra-infrastructure-development-working-group-report-2023-2025)).

The internet-of-things licence decree was adopted in August 2026; it authorises the grant rather than recording it, and no licence number, fee, coverage obligation or ownership of the licensee is published ([licence](2026-08-05-les-grandes-decisions-du-conseil-des-ministres-du-4-aout-2026)).

No subscriber, coverage or population-served figure for mobile service appears anywhere in this ledger.

summary: A [satellite licence](2026-05-19-le360-starlink-operationnel-dans-un-pays-africain-sur-deux) has not been granted twelve months after the operator listed the country as available, and [spectrum royalties for satellite and machine-to-machine services](2026-07-31-togo-conseil-des-ministres-30-juillet-2026-communique) were amended by decree.
developments:
The operator lists the country as available from 2026 with no licence granted; twelve months without movement is the finding, and the regulator has issued no statement on any application ([licence](2026-05-19-le360-starlink-operationnel-dans-un-pays-africain-sur-deux), [regulation](2025-01-14-togo-techs-tg-starlink-en-afrique-espoirs-et-regulation), [coverage](2025-05-07-togo-isoc-gouvernance-numerique-connecter-les-zones-oubliees)).

The royalty amendment was adopted in July 2026 and framed as encouraging innovation and connectivity; the parent decree is held only as an image scan with no text layer, so the baseline rates are unreadable ([royalties](2026-07-31-togo-conseil-des-ministres-30-juillet-2026-communique), [adjustment](2026-07-31-togo-ajuste-reglementation-redevances-radioelectriques-innovation-connectivite)).

Adjusting satellite spectrum royalties while granting no satellite licence is the sequence the record shows.

summary: [Capacity on a second submarine system](2026-07-15 CSquared boosts internet by integrating with 2Africa West cable) was added for route diversity, on a pan-regional account with no country-specific figure.
developments:
The country is one of eleven places tagged in the account, and no national capacity, price or route figure is published ([capacity](2026-07-15 CSquared boosts internet by integrating with 2Africa West cable), [fibre pair](2022-03-01 Liquid Intelligent acquires Google's fiber pair to improve offers), [ownership](2025-10-20 Redefining competition and submarine cable ownership Equiano, MainOne, and the making of middlemen)).

Route diversity on the subsea leg is real and unquantified here. It is the only international-capacity item in the ledger.

summary: A [national data centre](2026-06-02 SIN, ST Digital to deploy cloud services at Lomé data center) is certified to the third tier and wholly owned by a state company, with no commissioning date, capacity, utilisation or customer figure anywhere in the base.
developments:
The certification and state ownership are as reported ([centre](2026-06-02 SIN, ST Digital to deploy cloud services at Lomé data center)).

Nothing else about it is published. A tier-three facility in state hands with no capacity figure is the whole of the country's hosting record on the physical side.

summary: A [sovereign private cloud](2026-06-02 SIN, ST Digital to deploy cloud services at Lomé data center) is being deployed at the national data centre under a partnership between the state operator and a pan-African group.
developments:
The partnership was signed in June 2026 and no launch date, capacity or price is published ([cloud](2026-06-02 SIN, ST Digital to deploy cloud services at Lomé data center), [group](2025-08-12-st-digital-sovereign-tier-iii-data-center-techafricanews)).

No source relates it to the separate facility the same group had announced building in the country, so whether this is one project or two is unestablished.

summary: A [cybersecurity agency](2026-07-21-togo-luxembourg-appui-transformation-numerique-cybersecurite) and a [response team](2026-08-20-savoirnews-togo-cert-tg-piratage-comptes-en-ligne) operate under a [strategy for 2024-2028](2025-11-03-3000-jeunes-formes-reflexes-numeriques) whose text is not held, and [handled incidents rose from 39,168 in 2021 to 181,088 in 2024](2026-08-03-togo-confiance-numerique-ancy-incidents-2021-2024).
developments:
The agency was created by cybersecurity and cybercrime amendments of June 2022; the creation date rests on a one-line mention in a lender implementation report and the constituting amendments are not held ([agency](2026-07-21-togo-luxembourg-appui-transformation-numerique-cybersecurite), [training](2025-11-03-3000-jeunes-formes-reflexes-numeriques)).

The response team issued a high-severity alert on an active account-compromise campaign in August 2026; no incident-response profile, incident report, annual report or count of affected accounts is held ([team](2026-08-20-savoirnews-togo-cert-tg-piratage-comptes-en-ligne), [alert](2026-08-19-republicoftogo-ancy-alerte-compromission-comptes), [defence](2026-07-29-palakiyem-assih-chairman-cyber-defense-africa)).

The incident figures are endpoint years given by the agency's director-general with none for 2022, 2023 or 2025, no definition of an incident and no primary ([incidents](2026-08-03-togo-confiance-numerique-ancy-incidents-2021-2024)); the strategy running 2024 to 2028 is held at year precision with no document and no adoption date ([strategy](2025-11-03-3000-jeunes-formes-reflexes-numeriques)).

summary: Three [source-code licensing agreements](2024-06-20-kazakhstan-nitec-togo-atd-egov-licensing) for electronic-government software were signed with a foreign state agency in June 2024, and neither government published its own announcement.
developments:
They are known only through foreign business press and domestic trade press ([agreements](2024-06-20-kazakhstan-nitec-togo-atd-egov-licensing)).

No system name, deployment, value or deliverable follows them. Acquiring source code for government platforms is a substantial sovereignty decision, and the only account of it comes from the press of the two countries involved.

summary: [More than six million unique identification numbers and biometric cards](2026-04-23-togo-6-millions-niu-fin-2025) were reported at end-December 2025, a rounded floor rather than a precise count.
developments:
Enrolment campaigns ran region by region through 2025 and 2026, and enrolled, number issued and card delivered are one counter because the card is handed over at the campaign ([numbers](2026-04-23-togo-6-millions-niu-fin-2025), [platform](2026-04-27-biometricupdate-togo-6m-niu-mosip), [campaign](2026-01-23-identification-biometrique-zio-18-fevrier), [phase](2025-11-19 Togo Advances Digital ID Program With New Enrollment Phase in Maritime Region)).

The figure comes from the government's own second-half 2025 reform-implementation report, which is not held ([count](2026-04-23-togo-6-millions-niu-fin-2025)).

That the three stages collapse into one counter is unusually clean for this frame — most units in it report enrolment and issuance separately and cannot reconcile them.

progress: Mixed, six institutions authorised on the regional instant platform while the mandatory connection deadline slipped by three months
summary: [Six institutions](2026-03-06-bceao-six-acteurs-pi-spi-togo) are on the central bank's list authorised to open instant-payment services to the public, and the [mandatory connection deadline](2026-07-07-bceao-prolonge-delais-pi-spi) moved from June to September 2026.
developments:
Integrated, operational, committed and authorised to open to the public are four different claims across four accounts, and the counts are not one series ([authorised](2026-03-06-bceao-six-acteurs-pi-spi-togo), [institutions](2025-08-04-togo-7-institutions-pi-spi-bceao), [launch](2025-10-01 BCEAO Launches Instant Payments Platform in Togo with Three Banks), [sandbox](2025-11-18 BCEAO Launches Developer Sandbox for Instant Payments), [platform](2026-04-14-mixx-togo-pi-spi-uemoa)).

The deadline moved to 30 September 2026 for banks, electronic-money issuers and payment institutions and to 30 June 2027 for microfinance institutions; the extension source is union-wide and binds domestic institutions by construction, with no national report of it held ([extension](2026-07-07-bceao-prolonge-delais-pi-spi), [original](2026-04-03-bceao-adhesion-pi-spi-30-juin)).

Four incompatible descriptions of participation and a slipped deadline are what the record supports; a single participation figure would be manufactured.

summary: [Retirement allowances began digital disbursement](2026-08-04-togo-cgar-dematerialisation-paiements-allocations-retraite) in July 2026 with registration of payment details required by 31 August, and no alternative is stated for a beneficiary without a bank account, a handset or an identity document.
developments:
No beneficiary count, disbursed value or registration rate is published ([allowances](2026-08-04-togo-cgar-dematerialisation-paiements-allocations-retraite)).

A treasury interoperable prepaid card was announced with no launch timetable; two regional precedents exist but the central bank's own register counted only two treasury issuers at end-2024, which a three-state account does not match ([card](2026-07-24-togofirst-prepaid-cards-digitize-public-payments)).

The regional guide to electronic-money issuance by public treasuries settles closed-loop issuance, a dedicated escrow for holders' funds and a complaints route, requires tariff disclosure and sets no fee cap ([guide](2021-04-01-bceao-guide-emission-monnaie-electronique-tresors-publics-umoa)). A hard registration deadline with no stated fallback is the access question this unit does not answer.

summary: [Electronic-money accounts](2026-03-18-togo-comptes-monnaie-electronique-progression) were measured by the central bank to end-2024 and published in 2026, and [mobile-money subscribers and transaction value](2026-07-08-moov-africa-togo-mobile-money-services) come from regulator figures for the third quarter of 2025.
developments:
The central bank observation is two years old at the point of its publication inside the window ([accounts](2026-03-18-togo-comptes-monnaie-electronique-progression)), and the regulator figures reach the base relayed through a report on an operator product launch ([subscribers](2026-07-08-moov-africa-togo-mobile-money-services)).

A new wallet entered service in October 2025 with a partner bank under regional electronic-money rules, built on the operator's acquisition of a foreign fintech, with no user or transaction figure on file ([wallet](2025-10-15-gozem-money-entre-en-service)), and an operator extended its mobile-money services at a launch event in July 2026 ([extension](2026-07-08-moov-africa-togo-mobile-money-services)).

Neither uptake measure is current and neither product carries a figure, so the direction of use here is not establishable.

summary: An [instant international payment service](2025-10-31 Ecobank launches instant international payment service in Togo) launched with the country as its first market, a [full-service payment institution licence](2026-02-17-techcabal-semoa-bceao-licence) was granted to a domestic fintech, and a [cross-border payments platform](2026-08-19-wearetech-lideflow-esso-dong-djafalo-paiements-transfrontaliers) was profiled.
developments:
The bank-led service launched in October 2025 with the country as first market, distinct from the central bank's platform ([service](2025-10-31 Ecobank launches instant international payment service in Togo)).

The payment institution licence was granted under the regional instruction in February 2026; the source is captured as a paywalled newsletter body ([licence](2026-02-17-techcabal-semoa-bceao-licence)).

A cross-border payments platform founded in 2024 was profiled by a technology outlet, and no transaction volume, corridor count, licence or customer figure is stated ([platform](2026-08-19-wearetech-lideflow-esso-dong-djafalo-paiements-transfrontaliers)).

summary: A [national consumer-rights outreach tour](2026-08-19-atop-arcep-togo-consommateurs-savanes-droits) reached its seventh edition across August 2026, covering mobile-money fraud and service satisfaction, with no attendance, complaint or outcome figure published.
developments:
The seventh edition ran 3 to 28 August 2026 through the regions, with stages covering mobile-money fraud and consumer satisfaction ([tour](2026-08-19-atop-arcep-togo-consommateurs-savanes-droits), [fraud](2026-08-14-togo-arcep-bassar-mobile-money-fraud-consumer-rights), [satisfaction](2026-08-13-togo-arcep-atakpame-consumer-satisfaction-critique), [regions](2026-08-09-togo-arcep-consumer-rights-kozah-assoli-binah)).

No attendance figure, complaint volume or outcome measure for the tour is published. Seven editions of a regulator-run outreach programme with no published complaint series is the shape of consumer protection here.

summary: A [second birth-registration catch-up campaign](2026-08-02-togo-deuxieme-campagne-rattrapage-enregistrement-naissances) was launched in July 2026, and an [online civil-status certificate service](2025-12-16 Digitalisation - civil status act requests now possible online) is still a pilot in five communes.
developments:
The report of the second campaign gives two incompatible reach figures — 6,461 on the ministry's account against nearly 7,400 on the supporting organisation's — unreconciled ([campaign](2026-08-02-togo-deuxieme-campagne-rattrapage-enregistrement-naissances)).

The online certificate service launched in five pilot communes in December 2025 and remains a pilot on the record held, with no dated extension and no completion date for national rollout ([service](2025-12-16 Digitalisation - civil status act requests now possible online), [platform](2025-12-17 Togo Expands Public Service Digitisation With Online Civil Registry Platform)).

The 2009 civil registration law under which both operate is under review, with proposals due before the end of 2026.

summary: The [electoral register](2025-04-02 Municipal elections in Togo - revision of electoral rolls begins 7 April) was revised nationwide over two weeks in April 2025 under a presidential decree.
developments:
The revision ran 7 to 23 April 2025 ([revision](2025-04-02 Municipal elections in Togo - revision of electoral rolls begins 7 April)).

It is a register separate from the identity agency's system, and the two must never be summed. Nothing on the record connects the six million identity numbers to electoral registration, and no source states whether the two will be reconciled.

summary: A [single window for infrastructure mapping](2026-04-03-guichet-unique-cartographie-infrastructures-centipos) and a [national satellite-positioning correction network](2026-04-03-guichet-unique-cartographie-infrastructures-centipos) were launched together, and [urban addressing in the capital](2025-12-18 Urban addressing - modernisation effort) began modernisation.
developments:
The single window and the correction network were both launched at the capital in April 2026. No legal obligation to declare works, no user count and no data-governance or access terms are on file for the window ([window](2026-04-03-guichet-unique-cartographie-infrastructures-centipos)), and no cost, operator, subscription model or availability figure for the correction network ([network](2026-04-03-guichet-unique-cartographie-infrastructures-centipos)).

Urban addressing modernisation in the capital began after updating the geographic address database of thirteen communes, with no completion date, address count, budget or operator, from a single source with no update since ([addressing](2025-12-18 Urban addressing - modernisation effort)).

A positioning correction network is the piece of national infrastructure that makes precise addressing and cadastral work possible, and it is recorded with no operator named.

summary: [Digital cadastral submission was made mandatory](2026-08-14-togo-otr-mandatory-digital-cadastral-submission) from 17 August 2026 with no fallback channel stated, and [pre-2007 land titles are being georeferenced](2025-11-19 Georeferencing of land titles - a revolution for security and transparency in Togo).
developments:
No fallback channel, fee schedule, submission volume or data-protection basis for the cadastral record is stated ([submission](2026-08-14-togo-otr-mandatory-digital-cadastral-submission)).

The georeferencing field operation runs under the revenue authority's cadastre directorate, reported by the revenue authority itself, with no parcel count, budget or completion date ([georeferencing](2025-11-19 Georeferencing of land titles - a revolution for security and transparency in Togo)).

Making submission mandatory before the georeferencing that would give it a reliable base is the sequence, and the positioning network that would underpin both was launched four months earlier with no operator named.

summary: A [tax-exemption platform interfaced to the customs system](2025-10-01 Togo Launches Online Platform for Tax Exemptions and Waivers) became mandatory from 1 January 2026 after a three-month transition.
developments:
It launched in October 2025 with a three-month transition to mandatory use ([platform](2025-10-01 Togo Launches Online Platform for Tax Exemptions and Waivers)).

A single source, with no uptake, request volume or processing-time figure on file. A three-month transition before a mandate is a more generous phase-in than the cadastral submission or the retirement-allowance registration recorded elsewhere in this unit.

summary: A [commercial-courts reform bill](2026-08-23-togo-juridictions-commerciales-numerisation-togopresse) was adopted by the Senate in August 2026, alongside [Hague Apostille accession](2026-08-14-togo-commercial-courts-digitisation-apostille-convention) in first reading.
developments:
The commercial-courts bill was adopted by the Senate on 21 August 2026 and the justice minister committed to enforcement and capacity-building; no entry-into-force date, platform name or coverage figure was stated ([reform](2026-08-23-togo-juridictions-commerciales-numerisation-togopresse)).

Both bills were adopted in first reading a week earlier; neither text is held and no second reading, adoption or entry-into-force date is stated for the apostille accession ([bills](2026-08-14-togo-commercial-courts-digitisation-apostille-convention)).

Digitising commercial courts and joining the apostille convention together would make foreign document authentication and domestic commercial filing both electronic, and neither instrument can be read.

summary: The [education management information system](2026-05-04-gpe-kix-study-tour-education-data-system) is mid-migration with the analytical layer distinct from the collection layer, and a [pupil registration number platform](2025-06-01-togo-aide-memoire-dixieme-revue-sectorielle-conjointe-education) has no clear evidence of numbers issued.
developments:
The analytical layer is not the collection layer, so national scale cannot be claimed for it, and the same publisher gives two different start years ([system](2026-05-04-gpe-kix-study-tour-education-data-system), [integration](2024-11-05 Togo - Integrating DHIS2 with existing EMIS systems), [platform](2022-12-01-hisp-wca-dhis2-emis-togo), [factors](2024-04-08-gpe-itap-togo-enabling-factors)).

The pupil number platform was recorded as launched in 2023 by the ministry, with no clear evidence of student identification numbers found in April 2024; the two accounts are in tension ([numbers](2025-06-01-togo-aide-memoire-dixieme-revue-sectorielle-conjointe-education), [evidence](2024-04-08-gpe-itap-togo-enabling-factors)).

The school-census collection system is mid-migration to online data entry with a consultant recruited in 2023, on the state's own joint-review aide-memoire ([census](2025-06-01-togo-aide-memoire-dixieme-revue-sectorielle-conjointe-education)).

summary: A [national climate-risk data platform](2026-08-24-togo-adaptogo-climate-data-platform-togofirst) was reported available online in August 2026, and the source gives no launch date.
developments:
It was reported available as at 24 August 2026 ([platform](2026-08-24-togo-adaptogo-climate-data-platform-togofirst)).

No launch date, data source, custodian, update cycle or access terms are stated. It is the only environmental data system in this ledger.

summary: The [national public service window](2025-12-17 Togo Expands Public Service Digitisation With Online Civil Registry Platform) added twenty-nine energy-sector procedures with other ministries expected from January 2026, and a [digitalisation programme](2026-04-02-mae-digitalisation-services) ran a four-week sprint at the foreign affairs ministry.
developments:
The council of ministers adopted a decree on 26 August 2026 amending the investment-approval committee so that the approval procedure is handled electronically ([decree](2026-08-27-togoofficiel-conseil-ministres-apizf-dematerialisation)).

No usage volume or transaction count is published for the window, and nothing on file after December 2025 confirms whether other ministries joined in January 2026 ([window](2025-12-17 Togo Expands Public Service Digitisation With Online Civil Registry Platform), [civil status](2025-12-16 Digitalisation - civil status act requests now possible online)).

The sprint launched at the end of March 2026, with no published schedule for the remaining ministries and no completion criterion ([sprint](2026-04-02-mae-digitalisation-services)).

A volunteering agency application is live on or before July 2026 on the evidence of its own registration tutorial, and whether it authenticates against a national citizen account or mints a separate identity silo is not established ([application](2026-07-27-togo-anvt-lance-son-application-mobile)). Electronic document management at the finance ministry reached a further training phase ([documents](2026-07-07-togo-archives-gestion-publique)).

summary: A [georeferenced municipal census](2026-08-11-togo-golfe2-georeferenced-municipal-data-collection) runs from August to October 2026, linking households, businesses and tax position to location.
developments:
It was launched on 11 August 2026 running to 10 October ([census](2026-08-11-togo-golfe2-georeferenced-municipal-data-collection)).

No data-protection basis, custodian, retention rule or access arrangement is stated for a register linking households, businesses and tax position to location. The country has a data-protection statute and an operating authority, and neither is named in it.

summary: A [national-languages speech and translation model project](2026-07-14-togo-langues-nationales-ia) was presented at an international summit with four data competitions carrying US$40,000 in prizes, by a [national artificial-intelligence laboratory](2026-07-14-togo-langues-nationales-ia) on which the base holds one source.
developments:
The project carries targets only: no collected-hours figure, no released model and no completion date is on file ([project](2026-07-14-togo-langues-nationales-ia)).

The laboratory presented it at a summit in July 2026; the base holds exactly one source on the laboratory and its 2024 origin is established retrospectively from a 2026 report ([laboratory](2026-07-14-togo-langues-nationales-ia)).

A fifty-language model project run by a laboratory evidenced in a single article is the country's whole artificial-intelligence development record, and no source states how it relates to the continental coalition the ministry co-founded.

summary: A [fuel marking and traceability system](2026-08-02-togo-marquage-tracabilite-produits-petroliers) launched with the obligation already in the regulations from July 2026, and a [digital toolbox for small enterprises](2026-06-10-atd-boite-outils-digitaux-tpme) was launched with donor co-financing.
developments:
Neither the contract amendment nor the marking regulation is held, and no contract value, duration or data-ownership term is published for the traceability system ([traceability](2026-08-02-togo-marquage-tracabilite-produits-petroliers)).

The enterprise toolbox was launched during a national small-enterprise week, built with German development cooperation and co-financed by three European partners, with no user or enterprise count published ([toolbox](2026-06-10-atd-boite-outils-digitaux-tpme)).

Data ownership in a national fuel traceability system is the kind of term that decides who can audit the revenue it protects, and it is unpublished.

summary: A [national digital start-up association](2025-10-27-togotech-lancement-startups) was officially launched under the digital minister in October 2025.
developments:
Revenue and jobs claims are association-reported, and no membership, revenue or jobs figure has been published since launch ([association](2025-10-27-togotech-lancement-startups)).

It is the only start-up item in this ledger. Ten months after launch the base holds nothing further on it.

summary: About [3,000 young people were trained](2025-11-03-3000-jeunes-formes-reflexes-numeriques) in digital hygiene at a campaign in the capital in late October 2025.
developments:
The event date is inferred from a relative reference in a November 2025 report, so day precision is not established ([campaign](2025-11-03-3000-jeunes-formes-reflexes-numeriques)).

No curriculum, follow-up or repeat edition is on record. It is the only general digital-literacy activity in this unit.

summary: A [first cohort of corporate data-protection correspondents](2026-06-25-ipdcp-forme-premiers-correspondants) was certified after a three-day session, and a [European support programme](2024-01-01-ec-tgo-001-programme-de-soutien-a-la-transformation) runs to 2030.
developments:
The correspondents programme flows from the 2019 statute, and no target cohort size or timetable for later cohorts is published ([cohort](2026-06-25-ipdcp-forme-premiers-correspondants)).

The European support programme for the digital transformation of the economy was committed in 2024 at year precision and runs to 2030; the aid-transparency record is the sole account and carries no activity report ([programme](2024-01-01-ec-tgo-001-programme-de-soutien-a-la-transformation)).

Certifying data-protection officers inside companies is the mechanism by which a statute with no enforcement record reaches a controller, and one cohort is where it stands.

summary: A [district and school data-use project](2026-05-04-gpe-kix-study-tour-education-data-system) entered its final phase, concluding in November 2026.
developments:
The start year is inferred from a three-year description and is not published ([project](2026-05-04-gpe-kix-study-tour-education-data-system)).

It is the only research activity in this ledger, and it studies whether education data is used at district and school level — which is the question the education management information system's own mid-migration state makes hard to answer.

summary: A [community network](2025-05-07-togo-isoc-gouvernance-numerique-connecter-les-zones-oubliees) to connect 2,000 inhabitants was announced as imminent in May 2025, as a response to the absence of traditional operator coverage.
developments:
It was stated by an internet society chapter as a response to the absence of operator coverage ([network](2025-05-07-togo-isoc-gouvernance-numerique-connecter-les-zones-oubliees)).

Nothing since. A single village-scale community network, announced fifteen months ago and unmoved, is the whole of the divide-bridging record for this country — against a universal-service instrument that appears nowhere in the ledger.

summary: An offline-capable platform for reporting gender-based violence and routing victims to the nearest care point was piloted ([pilot](2026-08-26-afrikelles-lebenam-vbg-digital-livinglab)).
developments: An offline-capable platform for reporting gender-based violence and routing victims to the nearest care point was piloted ([pilot](2026-08-26-afrikelles-lebenam-vbg-digital-livinglab)). It is a pilot; no case volume or coverage is stated.

summary: [US$160m was approved](2026-06-24-world-bank-raise-electricity-access-togo-gambia) in June 2026 for electricity access in Togo and The Gambia.
developments:
The [financier's own release of 24 June 2026](2026-06-24-world-bank-raise-electricity-access-togo-gambia) records US$160m of concessional financing approved for the regional access and sustainable energy project, implemented with the regional commission under the West African programme.

The Togolese share is not broken out, so the figure states the size of the operation rather than what reaches Togo. No connection target or rural access rate accompanies it.

summary: Eight member states [approved a draft land registration harmonisation directive](2026-06-26-uemoa-directive-immatriculation-propriete-fonciere) in June 2026.
developments:
The [directive approved at Ouagadougou](2026-06-26-uemoa-directive-immatriculation-propriete-fonciere) harmonises land registration and titling rules across the union and covers the establishment of urban land information systems.

It is a draft approved by ministers, not a transposed rule, and nothing in the base records Togolese implementation of it.
